name: Italy: Piedmont

outcome.intro: After studying this section, a student will know the grape varieties, appellations, and styles of important Piedmont wines.
outcome.certified: After studying this section, a candidate will know the major DOCGs within Piedmont, know their grape varieties, understand their styles, aging requirements, and labeling laws. A Certified Sommelier will be able to recognize iconic producers and be able to sell and recommend food pairings with Barolo and Barbaresco to a guest.

rows.intro: On the border of Switzerland and France.
Mountains: Apennine Mountains, Alps, which provide a rain shadow. Piedmont refers to the foothills of the Alps.; Bodies of Water: Po River (Po River Valley)

rows.certified: Spanna: Local name for Nebbiolo in Gattinara and Ghemme.

rows.intro: Traditional aging in large barrels.; Aging requirements (law) exist for Barolo and Barbaresco.
rows.certified: Actual Requirements:; Barolo: 38 months total aging with a min of 18 months in oak.; Barbaresco: 26 months total aging with a min of 9 months in oak.

rows.intro: Barolo DOCG: Dry red wine from the Nebbiolo grape variety.; Barbaresco DOCG: Dry red wines from the Nebbiolo grape variety.; Moscato d'Asti DOCG: Off-dry, semi-sparkling white wine from the Moscato grape variety.; Gavi DOCG: Dry white wines, made from the Cortese grape variety.; Barbera d'Asti DOCG: Dry red wines made from the Barbera grape variety.
rows.certified: Barolo DOCG: Identify on a map. Know Tanaro River and Langhe Hills.; Top Barolo Vineyards: Cannubi, Brunate, and Monprivato; Barbaresco DOCG: Identify on a map. Know Tanaro River and Langhe Hills.; Top Barbaresco Vineyards: Ovello, Montestefano, Pora, Asili; Asti DOCG: Fully sparkling Moscato.; Brachetto d'Acqui DOCG: Off-dry, semi-sparkling red wine from Brachetto.; Alta Langa DOCG: Metodo Classico sparkling wines, min combined 90% Pinot Noir and/or Chardonnay.; Roero DOCG: Dry red wines from Nebbiolo grape variety.; Roero Arneis DOCG: Dry white wines from Arneis.; Ghemme DOCG: Dry red wines from Nebbiolo, locally known as Spanna.; Gattinara DOCG: Dry red wines from Nebbiolo, locally known as Spanna.

rows.intro: Nebbia: Local name of fog rolling off the foothills of the Alps.
All: Dry, sweet, sparkling, red, white

rows.certified: Barolo: Vietti, Giacomo Conterno, Bruno Giacosa, Ceretto, Sandrone, Elio Altare, Giuseppe Mascarello; Barbaresco: Gaja, La Spinetta, Produttori del Barbaresco, Vietti, Bruno Giacosa, Ceretto
Know the best vintages for Barolo and Barbaresco over the last 10 years.
Traditional vs. Modernist Barolo and Barbaresco styles.
Long range of ageability for Barolo and Barbaresco.
Big tannins require meat or fat.
